HxResult HxAppCapFindApplicationForExtn ( HxMIMEExtn_t  extn,
HxMIMEVerb_t  verb,
char *  appPath,
int32_t *  size 
)

: find the default application for an extention/verb pair

Given a file extention and verb, look in the app capabilities database and return the path to the application that is registered as the default for that pair.

Parameters:
extn IN: a file extention string (e.g. "html")
verb IN: a verb string (e.g. kHxMIMEVerbOpen)
appPath IN: a valid path to an executable
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if a registered appPath exists and is marked as default. Returns HX_FAILURE otherwise.

HxResult HxAppCapGetOneAppForExtn ( int32_t  index,
HxMIMEExtn_t  extn,
HxMIMEVerb_t  verb,
char *  outBuf,
int32_t *  pOutSize,
bool *  pIsDefault 
)

: Get one application for given extention/verb pair

Enable iteration over applications for a file extention and verb pair in the app capabilities registry by returning one (indicated by index) each time.

Parameters:
index IN: which entry to return (0-based)
extn IN: file extention for which apps are sought
verb IN: verb for which apps are sought
outBuf IN: the address of a char buffer into which to write the result
pOutSize IN/OUT:the address of an integer giving the size of outBuf when passed in, and on return either the size of the result or the size that would be needed to store the result.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if all's well. Returns HX_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL if an entry is found but it is larger that the buffer passed in. Returns HX_FAILURE otherwise.

HxResult HxApplicationGetIconForExtn ( HxMIMEExtn_t  extention,
HxMIMEVerb_t  mimeVerb,
HxApplicationIcon_t  icon 
)

fetches icon of app that handles extention/verb

Look up the default application for the given extention and verb, and return the full path to any icon registered via its .hxi file.

Parameters:
extention IN: an extention (dotless) (e.g. "txt")
mimeVerb IN: a mime verb string (e.g. "com.palm.open")
icon IN: buffer where path will be written on return
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. HX_NOT_FOUND if there is no app registered for the given extention/verb pair. If there is an app but it has no icon, HX_OK is returned but icon will be set to an empty string.

HxResult HxApplicationGetIconForFile ( const char *  path,
HxMIMEVerb_t  mimeVerb,
HxApplicationIcon_t  icon 
)

fetches icon for handled file

Using libmagic, determine the mime type of the given file, then Look up the default application for that mime type and the given verb. Return the full path to any icon registered via its .hxi file.

Parameters:
path IN: location of file whose mime type is to be used
mimeVerb IN: a mime verb string (e.g. "com.palm.open")
icon IN: buffer where icon path will be written on return
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful; HX_FILETYPE_UNKNOWN if the file's type cannot be determined; HX_NOT_FOUND if there is no app registered for the mime type/verb pair. If there is an app but it has no icon, HX_OK is returned but icon will be set to an empty string.

HxResult HxApplicationLaunchExtention ( HxMIMEExtn_t  extention,
HxMIMEVerb_t  mimeVerb,
const char *  path,
const char *  name 
)

Launches application to handle extention.

Look up the application that the user's set as default for the given extention and verb, and launch it with the string passed in mimeBuffer -- which will generally be path to a file to be viewed using the app. If there's no default app registered, just pick one. If there's no app registered at all, do nothing.

Parameters:
extention IN: an extention (dotless) (e.g. "txt")
mimeVerb IN: a mime verb string (e.g. "com.palm.open")
path IN: path to file to open (e.g. "/tmp/file7387237.txt")
name IN: user-visible name (.e.g "resume.txt")

HxResult HxApplicationLaunchFile ( const char *  path,
HxMIMEVerb_t  mimeVerb,
const char *  name 
)

Launches application to handle file.

Using libmagic, take a guess at the type of the file, then do a mime-based launch of the application that the user's set as default for that mime type and the given verb. Launch it with the string passed in name -- which will generally be path to a file to be viewed using the app. If there's no default app registered, just pick one. If there's no app registered at all, or we can't determine the mime type, do nothing.

Parameters:
path IN: path to a file to be typed then passed to launched app
mimeVerb IN: a mime verb string (e.g. "com.palm.open")
name IN: additional parameter, e.g. user-visible name of the file
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful; HX_FILETYPE_UNKNOWN if libmagic can't determine the file type; * HX_NOT_FOUND if there is no app registered to handle the type.

HxResult HxApplicationLaunchMIME ( HxMIMEType_t  mimeType,
HxMIMEVerb_t  mimeVerb,
const char *  path,
const char *  name 
)

Launches application with MIME information.

Look up the application that the user's set as default for the given mime type and verb, and launch it with the string passed in mimeBuffer -- which will generally be path to a file to be viewed using the app. If there's no default app registered, just pick one. If there's no app registered at all, do nothing.

Parameters:
mimeType IN: a mime type string (e.g. "text/plain")
mimeVerb IN: a mime verb string (e.g. "com.palm.open")
path IN: path to file to open (e.g. "/tmp/file7387237.txt")
name IN: user-visible name (.e.g "resume.txt")

HxResult HxApplicationLaunchScheme ( HxMIMEScheme_t  scheme,
HxMIMEVerb_t  mimeVerb,
const char *  path,
const char *  name 
)

Launches application to handle scheme.

Look up the application that the user's set as default for the given scheme and verb, and launch it with the string passed in path -- which should be everything after the colon in the URL that starts with the scheme. So if the URL is "mailto:foo@palm.com?subject=hello" the scheme is "mailto:" (colon optional) and the path is "foo@palm.com?subject=hello". The path string will be passed unmodified to the launched application.

If several apps are registered for this scheme but none is marked as default, just pick one. If there's no app registered at all, do nothing.

Parameters:
scheme IN: a scheme (colon optional) (e.g. "mailto:")
mimeVerb IN: a mime verb string (e.g. "com.palm.open")
path IN: a string appropriate to the scheme; typically, the string that follows the scheme in a URL: e.g. a local path for "file:", email address for "mailto:", web address for "http:", etc. Will be passed unmodified to the launched app.
name IN: user-visible name (.e.g "resume.txt")

HxResult HxMIMEDataGetExtention ( HxMIMEData_t *  data,
const char **  pStr 
)

extension from mime event

When an app's mime event handler receives a mime event, if the launch that triggered the event was by extension then it will include that extension. This function lets you retrieve the extension.

Parameters:
data IN: pointer to opaque type returned by a previous call to HxMessageGetData.
pStr OUT: const pointer to the extension, or NULL if there is none. Mime event elements are always converted to a normalized form to make them easier to compare. In the case of extensions this means that all letters are lower-case and that there is no initial ".".
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

)

pStr OUT: const pointer to the second of two parameters passed to the launch command via HxApplicationLaunchMIME, HxApplicationLaunchScheme or HxApplicationLaunchExtention
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

const char **  pStr

Returns:

HxResult HxMIMEDataGetReason ( HxMIMEData_t *  data,
AppCapsType_t *  pType 
)

Indicates why mime event was received.

An app's mime event handler receives an event because one of three functions was called: HxApplicationLaunchMIME, HxApplicationLaunchScheme or HxApplicationLaunchExtention. This function lets the application determine which, and so decide which elements to examine, what parameters to expect, etc.

Parameters:
data IN: pointer to opaque type returned by a previous call to HxMessageGetData.
pType OUT: The type indicating why the event was sent. It will be one of kTypeMime, kTypeExtn, or kTypeScheme.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.
